content:
- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too smooth, missing sharp spikes or sudden drops in the true outcome.
- After a spike in the history (e.g., 35.94, 36.62, 38.18), model overreacts with a lagged overshoot, then corrects too slowly.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — it overcorrects downward after a spike, then fails to recover quickly.
- Forecasts are often too low in the middle of the 30-day horizon, then rise too late — suggesting poor mid-term calibration.
- Model underestimates the true outcome in the last 5–10 days of the forecast window, especially when true values are rising sharply.
- Forecasts show a persistent lag in capturing the true price’s momentum — especially after a 30-day high or low.
